mcqs.question: A topic has several independently-owned consumer teams. What's the most reliable way to avoid breaking them when the schema changes?
options: Make changes backward-compatible by default and enforce that with a schema registry that rejects incompatible changes at publish time
Coordinate every deploy manually with each consumer team over chat before publishing a change
Ask each consumer team to add defensive null-checks for every possible field
Version the entire topic name (e.g. orders-v2) every time any field changes
mcqs.explanation: A schema registry mechanically enforces backward compatibility before a breaking change can ship, which scales past manual coordination and doesn't rely on every consumer team remembering to defend against every possible change. Renaming the topic on every change is far more disruptive than an additive-field approach and isn't how compatible evolution is normally handled.

mcqs.question: A producer renames `user_id` to `customer_id` in its event schema without telling anyone. What's the resulting failure mode for downstream consumers?
options: Consumers immediately throw a clear deserialization error naming the missing field
Consumers silently see null values for the field they depend on and produce quietly wrong output with no error raised
The broker automatically rejects the renamed schema and blocks the producer's deploy
Nothing breaks, since JSON field renames are always backward-compatible by default
mcqs.explanation: A silent rename produces no error at all — consumers expecting the old field name just see it missing (null), and their logic keeps running on bad data without any signal something's wrong. Without an enforced schema registry, the broker doesn't block this, and a rename is exactly the kind of change that is NOT backward-compatible by default.

mcqs.question: Before removing a field from a message schema, how do you find out which consumers still depend on it?
options: Assume no one depends on it if the field looks old
Check the producer's own code, since it will list every consumer that reads its output
Schema registry lineage/usage tooling where available, or a documented team convention tracking field consumers — the broker doesn't track this on its own
Remove the field and monitor for complaints from other teams afterward
mcqs.explanation: Because the broker has no built-in visibility into which application code reads which fields, you need either registry-level lineage tooling or a team convention that tracks this explicitly. Assuming based on appearance or checking producer code (which has no visibility into consumers) aren't reliable, and removing first and waiting for complaints is exactly the risky approach deprecation is meant to avoid.

mcqs.question: A team treats their event schema as "just JSON, an internal detail we can change freely." Why is that the wrong model?
options: JSON schemas cannot technically be changed once a topic is created
Only XML-based message formats require compatibility rules; JSON is exempt
It's actually the correct model, since internal formats don't need external discipline
In practice, the schema is a public contract with every consumer team reading that topic, whether or not it's formally documented as one
mcqs.explanation: Regardless of the serialization format, any field consumers rely on functions as a contract in practice — breaking it breaks real downstream systems. JSON schemas absolutely can change technically; the issue is treating that flexibility as license to change freely without discipline, and format (JSON vs XML) has nothing to do with whether compatibility rules are needed.
